thread:
ashwin: FYI we just got a Sev2 from ACME Corp — p99 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~2.3s for their standard chat route after yesterday's batcher config change. They see lots of 504/timeout-ish errors too.

maria: Ugh. Any repro steps from support? tenant id / example request?

ashwin: Tenant: acme-prod-12. Support pasted a single failing request: small prompt (~12 tokens) to /v1/chat/stream. They reported that requests get queued ~1.8s before we start streaming tokens.

carmen: Can you grab tail logs from the serving nodes handling that tenant? pattern looks like hold-window is accumulating tiny requests into big microbatches.

ashwin: Attached logs snippet from one pod: ```
[2024-06-12T09:12:11Z] REQUEST id=req-72 tenant=acme-prod-12 size=12
[2024-06-12T09:12:11Z] ENQUEUE batcher=continuous shard=3
[2024-06-12T09:12:12Z] BATCH_START id=batch-881 size=14 hold_ms=950
[2024-06-12T09:12:13Z] DISPATCH to-runtime latency=1832ms
[2024-06-12T09:12:13Z] STREAM_START token_count=0 delay_since_enqueue=1850ms
```

maria: That BATCH_START hold_ms=950 is the key. Default linger/grace windows were increased in rollout yesterday to improve throughput for large prompts, but for tenants with tiny prompts that increases tail latency.

ashwin: Support says this only started after the config flip -- confirmed. They also hit an auth 401 once; not consistent. Billing spikes are noise but we should focus p99 latency first.

leah: Quick triage: can we force-route acme-prod-12 to the low-latency path (max_batch_size=1 / hold_ms=20) as a hotfix? ops-bot can run route override? :pray:

ops-bot: /route-override set tenant=acme-prod-12 policy=low-latency max_batch_size=1 hold_ms=20 -> submitted to control-plane (req id r-83922).

carmen: Also add a temporary fallback policy: if queue wait > 200ms for tiny inputs (<32 tokens) dispatch immediately. That mitigates without touching global config.

maria: Agreed. For a longer-term fix we should: 1) enable tenant-aware batching heuristics (tiny-prompt fast-path), 2) add canary rollback for the linger increase, 3) add better observability: histogram of hold times by prompt size.

ashwin: Replication steps for eng-runtime: 
1) Start a small-load generator sending 10-20 req/s with 8-16 token prompts.
2) Apply the live config: continuous.batcher.grace_ms=900 continuous.batcher.max_batch_size=64.
3) Observe p99 on a single shard. Repro seen in ~3-5 minutes.

carmen: I tried repro locally, saw the same: average latency ok but p99 jumps. I pushed a canary that reduces grace_ms to 60 for tenants matching tinyprompt=true and that removed tail.

leah: Good. Next steps for Support: inform customer of temporary routing fix and ask if they can validate. Ask for any example traces and whether they observed auth 401 on the same time window.

maria: Also: add a regression alert that fires when p99 for prompt_size<32 increases >2x against baseline for 10min.

ashwin: Support updated customer — they're verifying and said latency improved immediately after the route-override. They will watch for auth 401 flakiness.

carmen: Follow-up item for infra: revert the global linger/grace increase until we ship tenant-aware heuristics. Filed RFC-4876.

leah: I can own canary rollback and the tenant routing playbook. tagging @oncall for overnight watch. :eyes: 

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigation applied (route-override), customer notified, ongoing monitoring.

ashwin: Thanks team — keep updates here if the auth 401 or billing anomalies correlate. If no regression by 12h we close. :thumbsup:
